notes.title: Massive Overhaul Update
notes.notes:
Hi, it's been a while! I'll go more into why in the "Status Update" portion, but first I wanted to cover what exactly this update is and why it was so important. 

Visuals
The visuals of the game were always a work in progress and bound to change.  I didn't plan on that change being this big.  There are still a lot of similarities in style and that approach, but the UI and rendering have both been overhauled not once but multiple times before landing on what it is now.  I made the decision to switch the game to forward rendering after a lot of thinking it over.  It was a switch that I personally believe made our game better.  We just weren't utilizing deferred rendering to its potential for this game and the frames saved in the switch helped a lot. We had also originally made every asset in the game ourselves, and when you are a really small team working for free, it gets hard and tedious to say the least.  That said we were able to integrate some lovely asset packs that really brought the game to a new level and were a complete gamechanger. I can say I'm finally happy with the look of the game and hope you guys are too.
tldr: 
UI was completely changed

Game switched to forward rendering (performance gain was too much to ignore)

Slight stylistic choices made to change visuals

Integration of some high-quality assets to compliment the overall aesthetic of the game.


Gameplay
To be brief... the game was basically stripped down and remade.  Thats as plain as it gets.



I can't stress that enough the game was entirely remade.  The base code everything was done on was just bad and that's entirely my own fault.  I was nearly new when this game started development and now have literal years of experience.  The game was just impossible to expand upon and waiting to fall apart like a ticking time bomb... and it did just that.  It fell apart and I took the LONG LONG LONG journey of remaking everything.  Along with the visual elements of course.  
tldr:
See line one under "Gameplay" ^

Entire Thing

The Whole Game

I'm tired grandpa


Status Update
Okay now to the boring part.  So, what is going on with the game now?? I'm actually almost done with level 3. Like I expect it to ship around Halloween (not actually intentional just happened that way).  


Why did this take so long?
In short... I've been busy man. With life.  When I started this, I was in college, had a part time job, and was single. So basically, I had a lot of free time on my hands.  Since then, I graduated, got a full-time job, started paying rent, and have a girlfriend lol. Working for free in my spare time felt less and less appealing as time went on and this whole thing just kind of faded into the background.  

Then suddenly things got a lot more normal once again and I had the time I needed. So here we are. 

I hate making excuses and sounding like that, but that's just how it is.  The rest of my team has been hard at work on other projects though, and there will be some updates on that to come! 

What I'm saying is, if you guys are cool with it, I thank you for being patient with me and this game.  It will get finished. Hope you enjoy this update and please let us know if there is anything wrong in our discord or on the google sheet that is now in game!!

notes.title: Update 0.1.4
notes.notes:
This update has a little bit of everything and a lot of internal testing went into it.  This came a lot later than I was hoping it would, but as a full time student and the sole programmer for the project it's a bit difficult.  As for the updates, I'll list some of them below.

Visual updates:

 Hedges were remade
 Grass was remade
 Some lighting and particles were updated
 Textures were updated to look more consistent


Gameplay/QOL:

 FOV and Gamma sliders were added to the settings menu
 Particles were added that trail the players in order to make navigating explored areas a little bit less annoying
 A few items were changed and a better functioning "quest list" was added to give more clarity on what to do in certain situation
 AI changes and a completely reworked death/ capture mechanic that feels more grounded in the world, but can still look somewhat cinematic


Optimization: 

 The hedges and Grass change also fits here as the new foliage has a much lower poly count, besides just looking better, and really helps performance.
 A lot of the structures were either remade or tweaked to lower poly count and help with occlusion.  This also had a large performance boost.
 Materials and textures were re-designed to lessen draw calls and reduce memory usage.
 Most of the code was went through and optimized further to reduce the weight on the CPU which should help frames.


There are more changes that have likely slipped my mind when making these lists and there were definitely A TON of bugs that took most of the time fixing.  With that said there are probably more bugs hidden in there that we were just unable to find so feedback is still very much welcomed and encouraged.  Thank you guys for all the feedback so far and apologies for the super late update.  Another update will come soon in the form of a progress update on the second level.

notes.title: Update 0.1.3 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
I said I would try give a dev log/ update weekly but was unable to follow through on that.  I've been sick and had midterms so that kind of got in the way, but I was able to improve a lot of things. With that said this is a bit of a bigger update compared to last weeks.

- Maze Monster AI has been improved again. I wanted to try something new and like it a lot more than it was before. She will now give some breathing room every once and a while to keep her from camping a single area.

- All the scare scenes where a monster catches you have been completely reworked.  Before they were a level sequence that would only play locally for each client.  There were some technical reasons for doing it that way and they did look a little nicer in my opinion, but the other players would either not see the monster or see the monster standing still during the kill.  Monsters now catch the player in real time using just rotations and animation montages.  It looks cleaner to everyone else and still looks clean to the player experiencing the scare.

- Items wouldn't respawn sometimes.  This was fixed I hope.

- Other graphical bugs have been worked out from what I can tell and should be working fine.

Like I said before I'll try and do a dev log soon, I may even work on that tomorrow since I'm on my spring break and starting to feel a bit better.  

Thanks for all the feedback guys this wouldn't be possible without it!

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.2 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
- Private Lobbies now work correctly and as do steam invites
- Crypt Crawlers have had their AI reworked to function better
- Removed the Recommended Settings on game launch
- The Gold Key no longer duplicates on spawn
- Rare Bug where players would get stuck in the death animation so they appeared laying down was fixed
- Maze Monster AI was updated to keep her from camping areas too hard
- Other general small bug fixes

I plan on making some dev logs soon and doing one update and/or dev log a week to keep everyone updated on the current state of the game.
